kereti.1#_: If they were cooked — l'chatchila one should not cook them in a meat pot intending to eat them with kutach; but if he cooked in a meat pot, it is permitted l'chatchila to eat them with kutach according to the plain language of the Gemara; and even if he transgressed and cooked them in a meat pot intending to eat them with kutach, we do not penalize him — Peri Chadash.
kereti.2#_: Well washed — and stam a vessel is well washed until it becomes known clearly that it is not well washed.
kereti.3#_: And there are those who are stringent — see Peleti, for I placed nearby to this from the Gemara, see there.
kereti.4#_: And b'dieved — this is when he already placed them in kutach.
kereti.5#_: To place them — even by way of pouring; so is the conclusion of the Acharonim.
kereti.6#_: Permitted l'chatchila when both are hot — it is like when they were cooked; and if the lower one is hot, Beit Yosef's view is that it is like came up, and Shach's view is like cooked, for the lower prevails; and see what Peleti wrote in siman 94; and Shach contradicted his words — here he wrote like Beit Yosef, and above he challenged — requires study.
kereti.7#_: It is clear to me, etc. — even though stam vessels are rinsed, this one that he wants to rinse is not in the presumption of being rinsed.

nekudot-hakesef.1#_: siman 95 s.k. 1 — on what Shach wrote in s.k. 1 that stam a vessel is well washed.
nekudot-hakesef.2#_: s.k. 2 — on what he wrote in s.k. 2 that the custom is to forbid l'chatchila.
nekudot-hakesef.3#_: s.k. 3 — on what he wrote in s.k. 3 regarding pouring.

yad-ephraim.1#_: Well washed — see Shach in s.k. 1.

peleti.1#_: Fish that were cooked — the law of fish that came up in a bowl is not comparable to fish that were cooked in a pot; see what I wrote in Kereti siman 6.
peleti.2#א: And the custom is to forbid l'chatchila, etc. And fowl meat — I am uncertain whether one should be stringent with it, since it is entirely d'rabbanan, or not; and it would appear that since Tosafot were uncertain whether they were cooked or only came up, and he wishes to bring proof from an oven plastered with tallow, etc., and he did not explain that kutach is different because it is only d'rabbanan — for Tosafot hold kutach is d'rabbanan as I wrote above siman 91 — that Tosafot hold in this there is no distinction between d'oraisa and d'rabbanan.
peleti.2#ב: Only came up, etc. And Shach wrote in s.k. 6 that one of them — the vessel or the fish — is hot, as Tosafot and Rosh wrote, etc.; and this contradicts his own words, for in the previous siman s.k. 33 he wrote there is no proof from Tosafot and Rosh if the lower one is hot — for Tosafot wrote for the master as he holds, etc.; and see what I wrote.
peleti.2#_: Both hot — see Kereti siman 6 and what I answered to Shach there.
peleti.3#_: Clear to me — see Shach s.k. 3 end.
peleti.4#_: Ash — see Nachalat Binyamin and Taz.

mateh-yehonatan.1#_: (Seif 1) Fish that were cooked or roasted — permitted with kutach when the pot is well washed.
mateh-yehonatan.2#_: (Seif 2) Egg — custom to forbid l'chatchila with kutach.
mateh-yehonatan.3#_: (Seif 3) Bowls — both ben yomo permitted when clear there is no clinging fat.
mateh-yehonatan.5#_: (Seif 5) Kutach and salt — do not place together.

yad-avraham.1#_: (Seif 1) Fish — noten taam bar noten taam of heter.
yad-avraham.2#_: (Seif 2) Egg in shell — Rashba; custom of Ashkenaz.

rabbi-akiva-eiger-yd.1#_: (Seif 1) On fish cooked in a meat pot — see Taz.
rabbi-akiva-eiger-yd.2#_: (Seif 2) On egg — see Shach and Taz.
rabbi-akiva-eiger-yd.3#_: (Seif 3) On rinsing — see Ran in Shach.

pitchei-teshuva.1#_: On fish with kutach — see sources in Kaf HaChayim.
pitchei-teshuva.7#_: On salt in milk bowl — Rashal.

kaf-hachayim.1#_: (1) [Seif 1] Fish that were cooked or roasted in a meat pot, etc. — and specifically if they were already cooked, b'dieved it is permitted to eat them with kutach; l'chatchila one may not cook them in a meat pot in order to eat them with kutach. Shach s.k. 3. Peri Chadash section 1; etc. And although in Beit Yosef s.v. he wrote that even l'chatchila it is permitted to cook in a dairy vessel something one wishes to eat with milk, it appears when Shulchan Aruch was compiled he retracted and was concerned for the words of those who forbid to cook l'chatchila; therefore he wrote in Shulchan Aruch the language of b'dieved, as Rav Yad Malachi wrote in Klalei Shulchan Aruch section 15 and Rav Chida in name of the Gedolim from forty books section 75 in Beit Av — see there. And all this is the ruling of Shulchan Aruch and Rama is stricter as he wrote afterward in the gloss to seif 2.
kaf-hachayim.2#_: (2) And accordingly it is forbidden to heat water l'chatchila in a ben yomo meat vessel in order to knead dough in them, because many times they eat bread with cheese. Dvar Moshe Chayei David siman 9; etc.
kaf-hachayim.3#_: (3) But if the vessel is not ben yomo — for it is noten taam lefegem and also noten taam bar noten taam, and it is a twofold leniency — it is permitted l'chatchila to heat water in order to bake bread. Beit David Chayei David siman 42. And although in responsum of Dvar Moshe there he was stringent also in this, nevertheless since there are many views that permit l'chatchila even with ben yomo, as Beit David wrote there — if so, it suffices with the stringency of ben yomo; but when it is not ben yomo there is room to permit, and so agreed Zivchei Tzedek section 4; and see below in the gloss seif 2.
kaf-hachayim.4#_: (4) And there are those who have a special vessel to heat water for kneading, and they do not use it for meat or milk — and it is good. Shulchan Lechem there.
kaf-hachayim.5#_: (5) And if he transgressed and cooked or roasted l'chatchila intending to eat them with kutach — nevertheless it is permitted to eat them with kutach, and we do not penalize him even if he transgressed intentionally, unlike Minchat Kohen who forbids. Peri Chadash; etc.
kaf-hachayim.6#_: (6) There. Well washed, etc. — and stam a vessel is well washed until he knows clearly it is not well washed, for stam vessels are rinsed. Shach s.k. 1. Knesset HaGedolah; etc. And see below siman 103 section 42.
kaf-hachayim.7#_: (7) There. Permitted to eat them with kutach. And there is no difference whether the fish are dry or moist, such as if they came up in gravy. Issur VeHeter general rule 34 end din 1; etc.
